newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk sees securitization savings.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk sees securitization savings.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said securitization of future revenues would save the company $200-$250 million by reducing the cost of borrowing to fund the restructuring of power purchase contracts with major independent power producers (IPPs).
The utility's investment banker has put borrowings at $3.2 billion to satisfy the pact with the IPPs.
Talks with the IPPs to convert the March agreement in principle into a definitive agreement continue, Niagara Mohawk spokewoman Kerry Burns said Wednesday.
Carol Murphy, executive director of the Independent Power Producers of New York, said the participation of water-powered IPPs is "a sticking point right now."
Burns declined to comment on the talks, but she and Murphy both noted that for several weeks the agreement has been described as "imminent" by participants and interested parties.

In a letter to shareholders living in New York state, Niagara Mohawk Chairman William Davis said securitization would allow the company "to secure a more favorable interest rate" by committing certain revenues to repayment of the debt.

Davis asked the shareholders to write to their representatives in the New York State Assembly urging passage of the Ratepayer Relief Act and repeal of the Gross Receipts Tax. The legislation is necessary before the securitization plan can be put into effect.

In a proposed letter to New York Assembly members, distributed with the letter to shareholders, the utility said the opportunity presented by securitization "will be lost if it is not seized during this legislative session."

"Securitization would improve the credit rating on the debt and reduce borrowing costs by an estimated $200 million to $250 million -- money that would translate directly into savings for consumers," the letter said.

Late last month, Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver told Reuters the Assembly "will not take up the (securitization) bill as presently composed." He said the bill "benefits only stockholders of the utilities."

Davis, in his letter, said the bills, both of which have passed the New York State Senate, "would make Niagra Mohawk more effective in a competitive marketplace and bring price relief to energy consumers in New York State."
After reaching agreement with the IPPs in March, Davis said the debt to be issued as a result of the settlement would be below investment grade.

The 17 IPPs owning the 44 projects covered by the March agreement are: Adironack Hydro; American Ref-Fuel; a partnership of Besicorp Group Inc and Kamine Development Corp; CalEnergy Co Inc ; Coastal Corp's Coastal Power; Cogen Energy Technology; Diamond Energy; ENSERCH Corp's Enserch Development; GPU Inc's GPU International; Indeck Energy Services Inc; International Paper Co ; Jones Capital; LG&E Energy Corp's LG&E Power; Mercer Cos; Oxbow Power; Salt City Energy; Sithe Energies Inc, which is partly owned by Marubeni Corp ; United Development Group; and U.S. Generating, a partnership of PG&E Corp and Bechtel.
